# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have learned that the required action is to cut the orange wire. Since I cannot speak or touch the bomb, I must pass this instruction through the Deaf monkey using gestures; the downward gesture indicates cutting, and the pinching gesture indicates orange.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🤌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch findings: keypad position 1 is engraved 0, position 2 is 4, position 3 is 1, position 4 is 7; no digits entered. Strip has an unpronounceable symbol, then the same other unpronounceable symbol twice. Display, light, and all six wires reveal nothing by touch.
Deaf says to Mute: Visual state: display 6; light blue; painted strip red yellow red; keypad keys 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7; one digit expected, none entered; wires in order 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.

The manual again requires cutting the orange wire. The Deaf monkey has confirmed that the orange wire is wire 6, while the Blind monkey can perform the cut but needs the instruction relayed. I will reinforce the cut-and-orange instruction to Deaf, who can tell Blind on the next opportunity.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🤌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 6; light blue; painted strip red yellow red; keypad positions 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7; one digit expected, none entered; wires positions 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display is now 0. Light remains blue; strip red yellow red; keypad 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit expected and none entered; wires red blue yellow green purple orange.

The manual still specifies the orange wire, and Deaf’s latest report confirms that orange is wire position 6. The display changing to 0 does not alter the manual instruction. I will send Deaf the established cut-and-orange signal so Deaf can relay the instruction to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🤌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display changed to 0; all other visual features are unchanged. Please state the manual's exact rule and required action for this bomb, including whether to press a key or cut a wire.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 6 and light yellow. Strip remains red yellow red; keypad 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit expected and none entered; wires remain red blue yellow green purple orange.

The manual’s exact rule is simply “Cut the orange wire.” It does not instruct pressing a keypad key. Deaf can see which wire is orange and can relay this verbally to Blind, so I will send the established cut-and-orange gesture signal to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "🤌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still cannot identify your two gestures. Please use the gesture code to tell Deaf to relay the manual's exact required key position or wire position in plain words, not just the gesture sequence.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 2 and light green. Strip remains red yellow red; keypad 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit expected and none entered; wires remain red blue yellow green purple orange. Blind gestured 🤝.

The manual’s exact instruction is to cut the orange wire, not press a key. Deaf’s view identifies orange as wire position 6. Because Deaf cannot hear, I will encode “cut wire 6” as the cut gesture followed by six identical count marks; Deaf can then tell Blind the required wire position in words.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not send two unidentified gestures. Send exactly one gesture for the required keypad position: position 1 thumbs up, position 2 thumbs down, position 3 OK, position 4 pointing up. If the manual requires cutting, send two gestures: first the wordless wire instruction by the same position code, then tell Deaf to relay that it is a wire.
Deaf says to Mute: Current visual state: display 6, light green, strip red yellow red, keypad 1=0 2=4 3=1 4=7 with one digit expected and none entered, wires 1 red 2 blue 3 yellow 4 green 5 purple 6 orange. Please state the manual instruction in words. Your new gestures were 👇 followed by six 👊.

The manual requires cutting, not pressing a key. The orange wire is wire position 6, but the supplied position-code alphabet only defines positions 1–4, so it cannot encode wire 6 without inventing an unsafe mapping. I will send only the unambiguous cut instruction to Deaf; Deaf can see that the orange wire is position 6 and relay that fact to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please speak the manual instruction to me in plain words. Tell me exactly whether to press keypad position 1, 2, 3, or 4, or cut wire position 1 through 6. Gestures are unavailable to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: display 8 and light yellow. Strip red yellow red; keypad 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit expected and none entered; wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. I received your gesture 👇.

The manual still requires cutting, specifically the orange wire, which Deaf confirms is wire position 6. I cannot speak to Blind, and the supplied position-code gestures define only positions 1–4, so there is no valid single position-code gesture for wire 6. I will resend the cut signal with a six-count marker for Deaf to relay verbally.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the orange wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You cannot speak. Gesture the manual's exact action to Deaf: indicate PRESS or CUT, then the keypad or wire position. Deaf must translate it into plain words for me.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: display 6, light blue; strip red yellow red; keypad 1=0, 2=4, 3=1, 4=7, one digit expected and none entered; wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange. Blind sent 🫵.

The manual requires CUT, not PRESS, and Deaf confirms the orange wire is position 6. I will send the established cut gesture followed by six count marks so Deaf can translate it to Blind as “cut wire position 6.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊"])
```
